item: A writer parked behind the swap window is pinned: the repair's BEGIN IMMEDIATE inside the window waits its whole 30 s busy timeout (30.065 s measured) when a thread that holds SQLite's write lock asks for a second connection or needs the gate the repair holds, then Declined(writer-busy), nothing switched; the gate rules out every gated writer (settings saves included) and a 136,587-checkout test sweep found no Core or raw writer opening a second connection

summary: Test and ledger only, no src change. Forced the cross-wait on the app's own engine (writer holds the write lock on a pre-window connection, asks for a second one in the window): the probe's BEGIN IMMEDIATE (busy 30 s) waited 30.065 s and failed, the window was held 30.066 s, the writer's second open waited 29.767 s in connecting(); the repair declines writer-busy, nothing is switched. Control (the writer touches its first connection again): refused as stale and invalidated, probe 0.33 s. A second shape (an ungated write, then any gated call while the repair holds the gate) is forced in the pin and not seen by the sweep. Mechanism for the shipped app: repair.run holds the single-writer gate for the whole window, gated writers (settings saves included) take the connection before the gate and hold the gate for their write transaction; the ungated corpus writers are the DDL and derived-store steps library_generation.py names, which run at launch and unlock. Sweep over the 1,506 test files it ran on: 136,587 checkouts, 103,477 nested, 668 under a connection that had changed rows, all ORM sessions, none Core or raw. Windows file-step variant (handles, 300 s, restore and repair) named, not exercised. Three order tests, mutation-proved (four mutants, each killed by the intended test). Ruled R338 a stated limit. Proposals for the user, neither built: connecting() refusing at once a thread that already holds a connection (recommended over the other, with a cost: a declined swap gives earlier connections their validity back, so the refusal would be spurious there); a shorter probe timeout (not recommended).
